g1-implement.title: #600: a gauge reading is named for the agent that produced it
g1-implement.imperative:
ONE gate, not three, deliberately: the writer, the reader and the engine must change together or the suite is red between gates, and a planned red window bridged by waivers is a plan smell (commander-core.md). Build exactly what ADMIRAL_RULING-1.md R1-R4 orders -- the ruling supersedes the frozen order's pre-rulings wherever they disagree, and PLAN_ALTERNATIVES.md candidate B is amended by it, not replaced.

R1 -- FILENAME AND FIELD, and the timestamp guard STAYS. Write the record to gauge-<owner>.json beside the spine, keyed on the LEASE session id, and also stamp an `owner` field into the record. The filename removes the collision; the field makes a mismatch detectable if one ever reappears. Do NOT delete or weaken #601's timestamp comparison in checklist_engine.py: identity handles the CONCURRENT case, time handles the SEQUENTIAL one, and a relaunch reuses its predecessor's lease name by design, so identity cannot see it. This wave does NOT complete decision:identity-not-time and must not claim it does.

R2 -- NORMALIZE, NEVER REJECT. Every lease session id must yield a usable owner key: SLUG PLUS HASH. 82 of 398 distinct session ids in this checkout fail the allowlist leg 1 proposed, because slash-bearing lease names are current fleet practice. Rejecting an unusable owner takes the governor away from a fifth of the fleet permanently and INVISIBLY -- losing the governor never fails a test. Reserve `skip` and `uncalibrated` as owner names so a normalized owner can never collide with SKIP_FILENAME/UNCALIBRATED_FILENAME (critic F4).

R3 -- NO LEASE KEEPS TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR. Owner-keying applies only where a lease exists. With no lease there is no owner, so read the unowned gauge.json and trip on it exactly as today. Fail-safe stays 'no attributable reading yields None'; it does NOT become 'no lease yields nothing'. Where a lease DOES exist and no owner-keyed gauge resolves, return None -- no fallback to the shared file, which would reinstate the folder-owned file this issue exists to remove.

R4 -- THE AMBIGUITY GUARD IS ABOUT ATTRIBUTION. In resolve_gauge_path (gauge_writer_hook.py:233), dedupe by resolved OWNER-KEYED path, write EVERY distinct candidate, and fire the len(...)>1 skip only when a candidate cannot be attributed an owner at all. Two spines in one work directory under the same owner still collapse to one file -- that is #488's own case and it must stay working.

ONE DEFINITION OF THE OWNER KEY (decision:one-owner-key-definition, a guess, not ruled). The key is computed on both sides of a process boundary: the hook from the binding entry's `engine_session`, the engine from its own active lease session_id. Drift between them silently stops every reading resolving. Define it ONCE in scripts/gauge_reader.py and load it in the hook through the by-path loader idiom this codebase already uses twice (gauge_writer_hook._load_spine_rail, checklist_engine._load_gauge_reader), keeping the existing fail-safe: a load failure yields no owner, which is today's behaviour and not a new refusal. If you depart from that, say why in the result.

CORRECTIONS THE COLD CRITIC LANDED, all accepted (CRITIC_TRIAGE.md):
- F4: the two sidecars use CONSTANTS (SKIP_FILENAME, UNCALIBRATED_FILENAME) on BOTH sides, so they do NOT follow the gauge name via .with_name(). Decide explicitly whether they go per-owner and state the choice; do not assume they follow.
- F5: _uncalibrated_advisory and _no_reading_advisory take base_dir only and sit OUTSIDE the trip region. Left on the shared path they would report on a file nobody reads. Name what each advisory resolves to.
- F11: tests/test_spine_rail.py (2 occurrences of the literal name) is the test of a FENCED module lane C is editing concurrently -- do NOT touch it; it goes to the Admiral as a cross-lane note. episodes/** are historical records and are never edited. Everything else in the blast radius gets an explicit change/no-change disposition in the result.

FIRST TASK, before any edit: enumerate BY COMMAND -- never by memory -- every artifact that asserts the literal name gauge.json (code, tests, docs, templates, skills) and STATE THE COUNT in the result. That enumeration is the blast radius and the author is the only one positioned to know it. Note that the literal name SURVIVES this change on the leaseless read path (R3), so 'zero occurrences' is the WRONG target -- each occurrence needs a disposition, not deletion.

REQUIRED NEW TESTS, by node id, because the four existing suites already pass and so cannot discriminate the healthy world from the broken one (critic F8). Create exactly these:
  tests/test_gauge_writer.py::OwnerKeyedGaugePath::test_two_keys_one_work_dir_each_keep_their_own_reading
  tests/test_gauge_writer.py::OwnerKeyedGaugePath::test_two_spines_one_key_one_owner_still_writes
  tests/test_gauge_reader.py::OwnerKeyNormalization::test_every_live_session_id_yields_a_usable_owner
  tests/test_checklist_engine.py::TripGaugeReadingOwnership::test_leaseless_checklist_reads_the_unowned_gauge
The second is #488's exact shape -- an Admiral's spine.json and its latitude-interrogation.json in ONE work directory -- and asserts the write HAPPENS. That regression cost an entire wave of dark governor and must not be re-armed by a rename (R4). The third must feed real session ids INCLUDING slash-bearing ones and the live null / literal '$SID' cases (R2). Run all four against the merge base a69bbac4 and paste the RED result; then paste them green at your head.

Evidence standard, inherited from tests/test_checklist_engine.py::TripGaugeReadingOwnership: red-before / green-after over BEHAVIOR, driving the real reader and a real gauge file, never a patched _read_gauge. Hook code cannot be validated from inside the session that contains it -- validate in a fresh process, never a fixture that hand-injects CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.

DO NOT fix measurement/probe_cross_key.py in this gate. After the change there is no gauge.json, so it takes its `after_sub is None` branch and prints 'VERDICT: NEITHER', which misdescribes the FIXED world. triage_candidates.statement: A SessionStart/stop hook tells a DISPATCHED CREW to drive its parent Commander's execute gate, because it resolves SPINE_FILE from an inherited environment. Measured by the g1 implementer: its own registry row records spine null, yet the hook named the parent's spine.json and instructed it to load constellation-commander, write STATE_NOTE.md and drive execute.json. Acting on it requires a --force takeover of a live parent's lease and would deadlock the wave -- the engine itself refuses with 'checklist lease is stale; claim it before mutating'. This is the SAME defect as #600 one layer up: a reading, a spine binding, and a hook's notion of which run it is in are all resolved from ambient context a dispatched agent inherits from whoever launched it. #600 fixes the gauge's instance; the hook's instance is untouched.

A Commander blocked on a foreground crew goes lease-stale while perfectly healthy. run_crew.py is blocking by design and a parent waiting on a child issues no mutating verb, so it cannot heartbeat: measured here, last heartbeat 13:20:19Z while blocked 53 minutes on a live crew, and the engine already called that lease stale. Anything that judges liveness by heartbeat -- recover_crews.py, any --force recovery path -- can therefore force-claim a spine out from under a running parent. Worth fixing before a recovery routine does exactly that.

A format-change enumeration and a dependency-change enumeration are different sweeps, and this gate's handoff only commissioned the first. The prescribed Wiring Grep for the literal name gauge.json could not find a dependency expressed as gauge_reader.py, so the installer's runtime-companion declaration was invisible to it; the full suite caught it instead. Left uncaught it would have shipped a DARK governor in every install -- the writer producing gauge.json while a leased engine read gauge-<owner>.json. Future handoffs that change a format should commission both sweeps.

why_trail.why: Execution context loaded and plan intent confirmed against the frozen order AS AMENDED by the ruling. The one thing worth stating before any gate opens: this wave fixes the CONCURRENT collision and does not complete identity-not-time, because a relaunch reuses its predecessor's lease name by design and no identity scheme can see that -- which is why #601's timestamp comparison stays.

Closed on leg 1's ACCEPTED artifacts rather than re-run, per the ruling's do-not-redo list. Candidate 2 is confirmed: the collision is ACROSS binding keys and the timestamp guard cannot see it, because a foreign write is fresh. That is why the fix has to be identity for the concurrent case, and why time still has to stay for the sequential one.

Owner-keyed gauge shipped: gauge-<owner>.json plus an owner field, slug-plus-hash normalization that is total, a leaseless checklist unchanged, and the ambiguity guard re-scoped to attribution. One flagged departure from R4's literal wording, taken conservatively and carried up rather than buried: with 2+ candidates under ONE binding key resolving to TWO DISTINCT owners, the crew skips instead of writing every candidate, because one binding key has exactly one transcript, so writing it to both files agent A's fill against agent B -- the #202/#261 fan-out dead end. R4's rationale (the writer could not tell WHOSE reading it held) is satisfied; its literal wording did not anticipate that third branch. The branch behaves exactly as today, so it cannot make the governor louder, and it reverses in one line.
